title: mHealth-AD: Training programme to promote the use of mobile health of mobile health technologies for people with mild dementia - Validation of the training programme
summary: The aim of the "mHealth-AD" project is to promote the use of mHealth technologies among people with early-stage dementia or after stroke. The project aims to expand knowledge about mHealth technologies and their applications, enabling both patients and caregivers to integrate these solutions into their daily lives. The goal is to support patients with dementia in maintaining their independence and monitoring their health status independently. To improve digital skills, an extensive training program is being developed, which can be delivered by professionals to patients or used for self-learning. The training program includes various materials for interactive teaching on the application and use of mHealth technologies. Information will be compiled in the form of documents and presentations tailored to the needs of the patients. Additionally, the training includes a Digital Serious Game. All materials will be made available on a digital learning platform. The training program will be evaluated in five healthcare facilities in Europe. The aim of the study described here is to test the materials with patients with dementia or after stroke and their caregivers to incorporate their individual experiences and needs into the development process. As has been shown for patients with mild dementia, the use of digital solutions may also provide support for stroke patients with spasticity. Although digital solutions are becoming increasingly important in healthcare, the actual use of mHealth technologies by patients after stroke, particularly in Europe, remains low. The results of a secondary retrospectively data analysis investigating potential predictors and risk factors for post-stroke spasticity in the clinical setting may help to identify high-risk patients at an early stage and facilitate recruitment for the mHealth technology.
